newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UNIONS EXTEND RAILWAY STRIKE 24 HOURS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UNIONS EXTEND RAILWAY STRIKE 24 HOURS.

text.p: The leader of the unions representing Czech railway workers said on Wednesday the national rail strike, scheduled to end at midnight tonight, would continue another 24 hours, the CTK news agency reported.
It quoted Jaromir Dusek, chairman of the Association of Unions of Czech Railway Workers (OSZ), as saying that OSZ's strike committee had voted to continue the action.

The OSZ, which claims that over 70 percent of the more than 100,000 employees of the state railways Ceske Drahy had joined the strike since it began Tuesday morning, is demanding a long-term plan for the loss making railways, which would protect job guarantees and sack the current management.

The conservative government on Wednesday has backed a hard line approach to the unions which took the strike action after the government was mulling a pla, which would have made deep cuts in the workforce in a long-term restructuring.

CTK also quoted Transport Minister Martin Riman as saying that a Prague court had ruled that the strike, the first major nationwide post-communist industrial action in the Czech Republic, was illegal.
Officials were not immediately available for additional comment.
